fields.description:
`docs/adr/` holds 83 files but only 61 distinct numbers. 17 numbers are reused — including FIVE
unrelated ADRs numbered 0037, all `Status: Accepted`, all flat in one directory. There is no index.
Meanwhile `AGENTS.md:42` cites "ADR 0025" by bare number and `CONTRIBUTING.md:173` sanctions bare
ADR references in commit trailers.

Design work established the cause and the safe remediation:

**Cause.** Every collision landed within ~3 hours median. But only 6 of 22 were true in-flight
Gerrit races; 16 of 22 were stale-base — the earlier ADR had already landed and the author never
refetched. A pre-merge check would have caught 16 of 22.

**Prevention is git's, not CI's.** A pre-merge uniqueness check on a monotonic counter is racy by
construction, and ADR 0047 explicitly accepts that a change may land without re-running CI after a
server-side rebase. The race-free mechanism is a per-number marker file `docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN`
whose content is the ADR's filename: two ADRs claiming one number produce an add/add conflict,
which Rebase-If-Necessary cannot auto-resolve. Empirically tested in throwaway repos: conflict iff
same number, ZERO false conflicts. A shared sorted index was tested and rejected — it conflicts on
EVERY concurrent addition (~23% of this repo's ADR additions would conflict spuriously), and a
contributor would resolve it by regenerating, silently producing an index containing both.

**Renumbering is approved** (limited user base). Earliest-landed keeps the number; 22 files move to
numbers above 0061. Historical disambiguation: ancestry alone resolves 23 of 90 commit references,
co-landing 40, topic-matching 86 — 4 remain ambiguous and only 1 resists human resolution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN` marker files exist for every ADR, content = the ADR filename
- [ ] CI asserts the bijection between ADRs and markers, and that no two markers share content
- [ ] A generated `docs/adr/README.md` index exists, grouped by workstream, showing full slugs
- [ ] `docs/adr/RENUMBERING.md` records the old-to-new mapping and the per-reference resolution table, with tiers marked and the unresolvable reference recorded as UNRESOLVED
- [ ] The 17 duplicate numbers are resolved, earliest-landed keeping the number
- [ ] Moved ADRs carry a "previously numbered" header; kept ADRs carry an ambiguity-window note
- [ ] `docs/gerrit-aws-setup.md:602`'s ADR range citation is replaced by an explicit list
## CURRENT-STATE CORRECTION (the header figures are stale; superseded here)

The description's "83 files / 61 distinct numbers / above 0061" reflects the board at ticket-creation
time. As of this implementation the ADR corpus grew (the sibling comment-triage shards 9ce8/4b94/ad16/ab77
landed NEW ADRs 0062-0069). Authoritative current state, re-measured from the tree:

- **91 ADR files**, 74 distinct numbers, **17 duplicate numbers** (5x0037; 3x0007, 3x0035; and 0008-0012,
  0015, 0016, 0026, 0031, 0032, 0036, 0038, 0040, 0041 doubled) = **22 files to move**.
- **Moved ADRs are renumbered to 0070-0091** (NOT "above 0061" — 0062-0069 are now taken by the landed
  sibling ADRs). Target range chosen to sit strictly above the highest existing number (0069).
- Tiebreak unchanged: **earliest-landed keeps its number**; the 22 movers are assigned 0070..0091 in
  ascending landing-date order (full git history, not the shallow-clone graft point). The exact old->new
  map is recorded in docs/adr/RENUMBERING.md and is the authoritative artifact for AC "resolve the 17
  duplicate numbers".

All seven acceptance criteria stand as written; only the numeric targets (file count, and the 0070-0091
destination band) are corrected here.
